findings.title: BVI BOI Penalty Moratorium Ended March 31, 2026 – Four-Tier Penalty Regime Now Fully Active
findings.summary: The BVI FSC's moratorium on BOI filing fees and penalties ended March 31, 2026. As of April 1, 2026, the full four-tier penalty regime is active with fines of US$10,000–US$75,000 depending on nature, duration, and impact of the contravention. BVI companies registered after January 2, 2025 must file BOI within 30 days of formation; pre-existing companies with late filings have been accruing penalties since April 1. The legitimate interest access regime also opened April 1, 2026, allowing AML-obligated persons to request UBO information for holdings at or above 25%.
findings.client_impact: BVI holding companies, SPVs, and fund vehicles that have not filed beneficial ownership information are in active violation with fines potentially reaching US$75,000 per entity. FGC must immediately identify any clients with BVI structures that have not yet submitted BOI and prioritise their remediation to stop penalty accrual.
findings.urgency_reason: Penalty regime has been active for four months; every day of non-compliance compounds the fine exposure. Immediate client outreach and compliance confirmation are required — this cannot wait for a routine review cycle.

findings.title: CIMA Publishes Final AML/CFT/CPF Compliance Rule and Sanctions Rule – Effective September 18, 2026
findings.summary: On July 20, 2026, CIMA published final binding rules on effective AML/CFT/CPF compliance programmes and on sanctions compliance, both effective September 18, 2026. All CIMA-registered or licensed financial service providers — including all registered investment funds — must implement expanded governance, risk management, compliance, and sanctions-screening requirements before the effective date. The AML Rule introduces certain requirements beyond existing practice.
findings.client_impact: FGC clients serving as directors or advisers to Cayman-domiciled funds and SPVs need to confirm that their registered managers, administrators, and CIMA-licensed service providers are on track to implement all required changes before September 18. Funds that miss the effective date face regulatory sanction from CIMA.
findings.urgency_reason: Effective date is September 18, 2026 — 46 days away. Outside the 30-day urgent window but close enough to require active monitoring; some compliance programmes may need several weeks to implement, making immediate vendor outreach advisable.

findings.title: Isle of Man Verification of Entity Registration Bill 2026 Passes Tynwald – September 15, 2026 Deadline
findings.summary: The Verification of Entity Registration Bill 2026 has passed Tynwald, reducing the UBO registration threshold from 'more than 25%' to '25% or more' and introducing more detailed, judgment-based control assessments for trusts and foundations. Nominated officers must adopt the new verification process by September 15, 2026.
findings.client_impact: FGC clients with Isle of Man companies, trusts, or foundations must confirm their registered agents or nominated officers are updating beneficial ownership records to reflect the lower 25% threshold and enhanced control assessments. Individuals who were previously just below the former threshold may now require registration.
findings.urgency_reason: Hard compliance deadline of September 15, 2026 — 43 days from today. FGC should contact Isle of Man–domiciled client structures now to verify their nominated officer is implementing the new process on time.
findings.source_name: Charterhouse Lombard / Isle of Man Government

findings.title: Brazil LC 227/2026 – Mandatory Progressive ITCMD Rates Nationwide by January 1, 2027
findings.summary: Lei Complementar 227/2026 mandates that all Brazilian states adopt progressive ITCMD (inheritance and gift tax) rates within the constitutional 8% ceiling by January 1, 2027. The law fills the long-standing constitutional gap on cross-border inheritances and donations and expressly subjects foreign-held assets to Brazilian ITCMD. For São Paulo-sited assets, the effective rate will move from a flat 4% to a progressive scale reaching 8%.
findings.client_impact: Brazilian HNW clients face an effective doubling of the inheritance and gift tax rate on São Paulo assets from January 1, 2027; cross-border structures involving foreign-held assets are also now expressly in scope. FGC should initiate succession planning reviews immediately — gifting programmes, trust funding, or inter-generational transfers executed before year-end may avoid significantly higher tax cost.
findings.urgency_reason: Implementation deadline is January 1, 2027 — approximately five months away. The planning window is actively narrowing: restructuring trusts, finalising gifts, or redomiciling assets can take months. Client outreach should begin now.

findings.title: US Treasury and IRS Post 2026 Regulatory Agenda for OBBBA Implementation – $15M Permanent Estate/Gift Exemption
findings.summary: On July 3, 2026, the US Treasury published its 2026 Agency Rule List outlining guidance needed to implement the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA). Key items include Revenue Procedure 2026-25 on new 'Trump Account' contributions and anticipated guidance on the new permanent $15 million estate and gift tax exemption.
findings.client_impact: US-connected HNW clients now benefit from a permanent $15 million individual estate and gift tax exemption (up to $30 million per married couple), significantly expanding wealth transfer capacity without gift or estate tax. Clients who previously structured estates around a lower exemption should revisit their plans to maximise the opportunity — irrevocable trust funding, GRATs, and direct gifting should all be reviewed.
findings.urgency_reason: The $15M exemption is already enacted law; Treasury guidance is being released in stages throughout 2026. Clients should begin estate plan reviews now rather than waiting for all guidance to finalise, as planning timelines for complex structures (SLATs, QPRTs, GRATs) can span months.

findings.title: Switzerland Federal UBO Register (LETA) – Effective October 1, 2026; Regulatory Optimisation Working Group Launched
findings.summary: On July 1, 2026, FINMA welcomed a Swiss government working group to optimise financial market regulation, potentially rationalising Swiss financial rules over the next 12–24 months. The initiative follows the separately enacted Federal UBO Register (LETA, effective October 1, 2026), which requires Swiss legal entities to register their ultimate beneficial owners.
findings.client_impact: Swiss-domiciled holding companies, operating entities, and certain fiduciary arrangements used by FGC's HNW clients must assess their LETA registration obligations and complete filings before October 1, 2026. The regulatory optimisation initiative may ease future compliance burden but does not affect or delay LETA.
findings.urgency_reason: LETA effective October 1, 2026 — 59 days away. Clients with Swiss structures should confirm registration requirements with Swiss legal counsel now to allow adequate lead time for gathering UBO information and completing filings.

findings.title: FINMA Revised AML Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA) – Consultation Closed June 2026, Final Rules Pending
findings.summary: FINMA's consultation on the revised AMLO-FINMA closed June 9, 2026. The revision strengthens requirements for understanding client structure, introduces rules on payable-through and sub-accounts, and adds new sanctions and embargo compliance obligations under the Embargo Act. Final ordinance expected later in 2026, calibrated to Switzerland's FATF mutual evaluation in 2027.
findings.client_impact: FGC clients using Swiss intermediaries, trust companies, or portfolio managers will face enhanced onboarding documentation, periodic review requirements, and tighter controls on complex ownership structures when the final AMLO-FINMA is published. Clients with layered or opaque holding structures domiciled through Swiss entities should begin a pre-emptive review of their documentation now.
findings.urgency_reason: Final ordinance expected in H2 2026. Early review of Swiss-structured relationships is advisable given the likelihood of increased documentation requirements — particularly for clients with sub-accounts or multi-layered structures.

findings.title: Panama Agreement 1-2026 – UBO Threshold Reduced to 10%, Full Chain-of-Ownership Mandatory
findings.summary: Panama's Superintendency of Banks issued Agreement 1-2026, reducing the UBO identification threshold from 25% to 10% ownership or effective control, and requiring documentation of the full chain of ownership to the ultimate natural person. Digital identity verification processes are also regulated. The Agreement reflects Panama's post-FATF grey-list obligations.
findings.client_impact: FGC clients with Panama-incorporated holding companies, SPVs, or investment vehicles must immediately review their ownership registers to identify any beneficial owner at or above 10% who has not yet been documented and verified. Gaps in chain-of-ownership documentation could impact banking relationships and fund access for Panama-structured entities.
findings.urgency_reason: Effective January 2026 (ongoing obligation now in effect). Given Panama's post-grey-list scrutiny, banks and administrators are actively enforcing the new threshold; non-compliant structures risk account restrictions or loss of service relationships.

findings.title: Luxembourg AIFMD II Implementation Deadline Passed – April 16, 2026; Transposition Law Pending
findings.summary: Luxembourg was required to implement AIFMD II (Directive (EU) 2024/927) by April 16, 2026. The directive introduces new rules on delegation and substance, liquidity management tools, depositary requirements, and loan-originating AIFs. Luxembourg's domestic transposition law is expected to affect fund managers using Luxembourg-domiciled structures for delegation and reverse solicitation arrangements.
findings.client_impact: FGC clients using Luxembourg AIFs or investing through Luxembourg-domiciled fund structures should confirm with their fund managers that AIFMD II compliance assessments are complete, particularly regarding delegation chain substance and liquidity management tool implementation. Reverse solicitation arrangements may face heightened scrutiny once the transposition law is enacted.
findings.urgency_reason: EU-level deadline passed in April 2026; Luxembourg transposition law is imminent. Fund managers who have not yet assessed their AIFMD II compliance posture are at increasing risk of regulatory challenge as Luxembourg implements.

findings.title: EU AMLA Publishes Draft RTS on Group-Wide AML/CFT Policies – Single Rulebook Applies July 10, 2027
findings.summary: The European Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA), which assumed all AML/CFT mandates from the EBA in January 2026, published draft Regulatory Technical Standards on minimum requirements for group-wide AML/CFT policies, procedures, and controls by its July 10, 2026 deadline. These binding standards form part of AMLA's Single Rulebook, applicable across all 27 EU member states from July 10, 2027. Luxembourg, Malta, and Cyprus wealth management structures are directly in scope.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients using EU-domiciled holding companies, investment funds, or trust equivalents in Luxembourg, Malta, or Cyprus should expect uniform, heightened AML/CFT documentation and governance requirements from their EU-based service providers from mid-2027. FGC clients in scope should anticipate more rigorous periodic reviews and enhanced UBO documentation standards.
findings.urgency_reason: Single Rulebook applies July 10, 2027. With draft RTS published now, EU financial institutions have approximately 12 months to implement; early planning and client communication will reduce disruption as the July 2027 effective date approaches.

findings.title: Cayman CRS 2025 Filing Deadline July 31, 2026 – DITC Portal Closure and Schema Transition to CRS 3.0
findings.summary: Cayman Financial Institutions were required to file their 2025 CRS Returns and Declarations by July 31, 2026 (now passed). The DITC Portal will temporarily close in early August 2026 for the transition from CRS XML Schema v2.0 to v3.0. The next CRS reporting deadline for the 2026 period shifts to June 30, 2027; DITC is expected to release updated CRS 3.0 guidance in Q3 2026.
findings.client_impact: FGC clients with Cayman-domiciled funds or financial accounts should confirm that their Cayman Financial Institution filed CRS Returns on time before July 31. The schema upgrade is administrative and will be handled by financial institutions and their reporting agents ahead of the 2027 cycle.
findings.urgency_reason: Filing deadline passed July 31, 2026. No further client action required on 2025 reporting; schema transition is managed by FIs. Note for ongoing monitoring: CRS 3.0 guidance expected Q3 2026.

findings.title: BCB New Capital Requirement Phase-In Begins July 1, 2026
findings.summary: As of July 1, 2026, Brazilian financial institutions began phasing in new capital thresholds under updated BCB regulations: 25% of the incremental requirement by December 2026, 50% by June 2027, 75% by December 2027, and full compliance by January 2028. The staged transition may modestly affect lending conditions at Brazilian banks.
findings.client_impact: FGC clients with Brazilian bank-sourced financing — including real estate leverage, company acquisition loans, or structured credit — should monitor whether tightening capital ratios at their Brazilian lenders affect credit availability or cost during the 2026–2028 phase-in period.
findings.urgency_reason: Phase-in is gradual through January 2028 with no immediate client action required. Relevant background context for clients managing Brazilian leverage strategies.

findings.title: Brazil 10% Dividend Withholding Tax on Large Distributions – Effective January 2026
findings.summary: Law 15.270/2025 (effective January 2026) imposes a 10% withholding tax on dividends exceeding R$50,000 in a single month paid to domestic individuals, and on all dividends paid to non-residents regardless of amount. This reverses Brazil's long-standing dividend exemption.
findings.client_impact: FGC clients holding Brazilian operating companies, private equity interests, or real-estate funds should ensure their dividend distributions since January 2026 have been restructured to account for the 10% withholding cost, and that non-resident shareholders are receiving net payments with correct withholding applied.
findings.urgency_reason: Already effective law since January 2026. Flagged as FYI given several months have elapsed since enactment; immediate client impact is limited to those who have not yet adapted. If any FGC client has not addressed this, it becomes an active compliance gap requiring urgent remediation.

findings.title: MAS Issues Risk-Proportionate Source of Wealth Guidance – Circular AMLD 05/2026 (May 25, 2026)
findings.summary: MAS issued Circular AMLD 05/2026 guiding financial institutions to adopt risk-tiered, proportionate SOW documentation, with simplified verification for established referrals and accelerated onboarding for clients with transparent wealth structures. Target: private banking onboarding under one month by end-2026.
findings.client_impact: FGC clients opening Singapore private banking accounts or onboarding with Singapore-licensed wealth managers may benefit from faster account opening and reduced documentation burden, particularly for clients with clearly documented wealth structures or referrals from established relationships.
findings.urgency_reason: Positive regulatory development reducing onboarding friction; no compliance action required from clients. Useful context for clients or referral partners experiencing Singapore account opening delays.

findings.title: MAS Consults on CIS Code Amendments for New Retail Fund Types (July 9, 2026)
findings.summary: MAS published a consultation paper on July 9, 2026 proposing CIS Code amendments to enable a wider range of retail fund types through a streamlined authorisation process, including products that may not fit existing investment guidelines, with appropriate retail safeguards maintained.
findings.client_impact: FGC clients evaluating Singapore as a fund domicile alongside Cayman or Luxembourg should monitor this consultation, as approved outcomes could create additional fund vehicle options with faster regulatory approval pathways in Singapore.
findings.urgency_reason: Consultation paper with no immediate deadline for FGC clients. Outcome expected in late 2026 or 2027; relevant for longer-term fund domicile planning.

findings.title: Luxembourg Carried Interest Tax Regime Modernised – Effective Fiscal Year 2026
findings.summary: Adopted January 22, 2026, the new Luxembourg carried interest regime taxes contractual carry as extraordinary income at one quarter of the global rate (maximum 11.45%), while participation-linked carry qualifies for capital gains exemption if the AIF participation is held over six months and does not exceed 10%. The regime covers employees, advisers, board members, and consultants involved in AIF management.
findings.client_impact: FGC clients who are Luxembourg fund managers, investment advisers, or board members with carried interest entitlements should confirm with their Luxembourg tax advisers that their carry documentation and tax treatment aligns with the new regime for fiscal year 2026. Both contractual and participation-linked structures need assessment.
findings.urgency_reason: Already effective for fiscal year 2026. Tax advisers managing Luxembourg fund manager compensation structures should have assessed this by now; flagged for any client not yet reviewed.

findings.title: Malta FIAU Amends AML Regulations – Legal Notices 82 and 83 of 2026
findings.summary: The FIAU introduced significant amendments to the PMLFTR and CBAR Regulations via Legal Notices 82 and 83 of 2026, adding periodic penalty payments for persistent AML/CFT deficiencies and enhanced supervisory enforcement tools reflecting Malta's post-FATF grey-list strengthening obligations.
findings.client_impact: FGC clients using Malta-licensed fund administrators, holding company service providers, or licensed investment service providers should expect heightened FIAU supervisory activity and potentially more documentation requests as Malta demonstrates enhanced enforcement capability. Malta-domiciled structures warrant proactive compliance reviews.
findings.urgency_reason: Already in effect since April 2026. Awareness item for clients using Malta as a holding or fund jurisdiction; no immediate client action required, but signals a more enforcement-active FIAU environment.

findings.title: CRS Amendments Applicable from January 1, 2026 – Scope Extended to Electronic Money and Digital Assets
findings.summary: OECD amendments to the CRS, adopted August 2022, are now applicable from January 1, 2026, extending reporting scope to electronic money products and central bank digital currencies. CRS XML Schema 3.0 for actual exchange is scheduled for 2027; 68% of jurisdictions plan to exchange under the amended standard from that date.
findings.client_impact: FGC clients holding significant electronic money balances or digital assets within CRS-reportable financial accounts (including Cayman and other offshore accounts) should confirm with their financial institutions that amended CRS reporting is being applied correctly to digital asset positions from 2026 onward.
findings.urgency_reason: Already applicable since January 1, 2026; the 2027 XML 3.0 transition is administrative. Relevant for clients with crypto or e-money exposure within reportable accounts who have not yet verified their FI's amended reporting coverage.

findings.title: DIFC Variable Capital Company (VCC) Regulations 2026 Introduced
findings.summary: The DIFC introduced VCC Regulations 2026, establishing NAV-based share capital, umbrella and cell fund structures, asset ring-fencing between cells, and a flexible framework for proprietary investment vehicles within DIFC. The VCC is aimed at family office and private equity use cases requiring segregated compartments and flexible capital management.
findings.client_impact: FGC clients exploring UAE-domiciled wealth structures or regional family office consolidation now have access to a flexible, ring-fenced multi-cell vehicle as an alternative to Cayman SPCs or Singapore VCCs. This is particularly relevant for clients consolidating Middle Eastern investment holdings or establishing UAE-based family investment offices.
findings.urgency_reason: New regulatory option in effect since 2026; no immediate compliance obligation. Relevant for clients in the planning phase for UAE-based or regional wealth structures.

findings.title: Trusts (Jersey) Amendment Law 2026 – In Force March 20, 2026
findings.summary: The Trusts (Jersey) Amendment Law 2026 came into force March 20, 2026, clarifying beneficiaries' right to terminate a trust under the rule in Saunders v Vautier and updating priority rules for claims between trustees and secured lenders. The amendments address uncertainties from the Rusnano Guernsey decision and Z Trusts litigation.
findings.client_impact: FGC clients with existing Jersey trust structures should ask their trustees to confirm whether any trust terms or deed provisions should be updated in light of the clarified Saunders v Vautier rules — particularly for trusts where all beneficiaries could theoretically elect to terminate. The trustee/secured lender priority changes are relevant for leveraged structures held within Jersey trusts.
findings.urgency_reason: In force since March 2026; no urgent compliance deadline. A trust review with Jersey counsel is advisable if clients have not yet assessed the impact of the amended law on their specific structures.

findings.title: Bahamas Central Bank Releases TF and PF National Risk Assessments – CFATF Mutual Evaluation Scheduled Q4 2026
findings.summary: The Central Bank of The Bahamas released the Summary of Findings of the Terrorist Financing NRA 2024 and the Proliferation Financing NRA 2025 in July 2026. The Bahamas CFATF Mutual Evaluation is also scheduled for Q4 2026, which may result in updated regulatory requirements for supervised financial institutions.
findings.client_impact: FGC clients using Bahamian-licensed entities, fund administrators, or custodians should be aware that the Q4 2026 CFATF evaluation may trigger updated AML/CFT compliance requirements in late 2026 or early 2027. Service providers may pre-emptively tighten documentation requirements ahead of the evaluation.
findings.urgency_reason: Q4 2026 evaluation is several months away; no immediate client action required. Awareness item for clients with Bahamas-domiciled structures or relationships with Bahamas-licensed service providers.

findings.title: OECD Pillar Two – US SbS Safe Harbor Active; GIR Filings Due June 30, 2026
findings.summary: The OECD Pillar Two Side-by-Side Safe Harbor, agreed January 5, 2026, exempts US-parented multinational groups from the IIR and UTPR for fiscal years beginning on or after January 1, 2026. GloBE Information Return filings for calendar-year taxpayers were due June 30, 2026. Approximately 140 jurisdictions have enacted or are implementing the 15% global minimum tax.
findings.client_impact: FGC clients managing US-parented multinational structures should confirm their GIR was filed by June 30, 2026 and assess any residual UTPR exposure in jurisdictions outside the SbS safe harbor. Non-US-parented multinationals with operations in Pillar Two jurisdictions remain subject to top-up taxes and must assess their effective tax rate jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction.
findings.urgency_reason: GIR deadline has passed. Ongoing monitoring item for clients with multinational corporate structures operating across low-tax jurisdictions — particularly relevant for clients with Cayman, BVI, or zero-tax holding structures feeding into Pillar Two-enacted jurisdictions.

discarded_findings_note: One raw finding was discarded as outside FGC's practice areas: 'FINMA Publishes New Liquidity Ordinance for Banks and Securities Firms' (Switzerland) — this is banking prudential/liquidity regulation for Swiss banks and securities firms, not directly affecting wealth management clients or FGC's advisory practice.
